column2: A call to a repository C/C++ macro links the caller to the functions the macro calls
C++ method calls resolve through declared receiver types, TEST_F fixtures and arity
`uses` with a regex character in the name answers with git's error instead of the matches
A graph miss is logged when grep searches a single file (its output has no file name)
A graph miss names the enclosing C/C++ function of each match, not an empty string
A code search is answered by the read tool that answers its question: a name inside one file gets that file's uses, a definitions listing gets the outline
A search for a field or dictionary key is answered from the keys and fields the graph records (#148), not only from symbols
A definition search with -A/-B/-C before -v, -c or -l is denied and answered with the body, though grep was asked for inverted lines, a count or a file list
A search limited by --include / Grep glob / Grep type to another language is denied with the answer for code it excludes
A graph built before a new caller or a second definition was added still replaces grep, saying the stale answer is the search's result
A definition search in a file edited since the build is denied with the caller pack, whose 'Defined at' line is wrong
A case-sensitive grep for a name that differs in case from the symbol is denied with the other symbol's callers
grep -e A -e B is denied with an answer for A only
A basic-regex or -F grep with a literal '|' is split into names and denied with their packs, though grep finds nothing
Definition searches devkb cannot answer in one file or with -A/-B/-C are no longer recorded as graph misses
devkb guardrail-stats leaves out read-answer and span-hint decisions
devkb guardrail-stats --project counts decisions from every repository
devkb stats counts every `uses` text-match answer as complete
The read-answer's location line is repository-relative, not the path grep prints from a subdirectory
A call reached through a package re-export that the resolver leaves unattributed is no longer counted, so the pack says Complete with no caller and no test
A dataclass field named like a function makes calls to that function unresolved (same file and cross-file), losing CALLS edges and the tests they lead to
Build time grows quadratically with typed-receiver calls: 400 small files take 81 s instead of 6 s
A module with many constants builds quadratically: 20,000 constants take 11.3 s instead of 0.85 s
`pack change` on a module constant says Complete with 0 functions and 0 tests while a test-covered function reads it
`pack refactor` (the command AGENTS.md names for a change) ignores a constant's uses and says Complete with no users
A read of a module constant from a function that declares it `global` is not attributed (lazy-singleton pattern), and `pack change` says Complete with 0 uses
A class-body name that shadows a module constant is attributed to the module constant
Constants assigned by tuple unpacking (`HOST, PORT = ...`) are not extracted
`symbol KEY` hides a string key's reads and writes whenever any symbol merely starts with the key
String-key reads miss `"k" in d` and the read in `d["k"] += 1`, and count `os.environ.get("k")` as a record-key read
#115 is only half done: `symbol` and `outline` still give two C++ overloads one merged range and print both bodies
`pack refactor` still answers "cannot resolve ... Search the code." with nothing, while `pack change` gives the text matches (#131 item 3)
One malformed model answer aborts the whole triage/handle/feedback run and is retried and paid for first on every later run
A transient GitHub error after a feedback ticket is filed makes the next run file the same ticket again; in triage it leaves an item labelled triaged with no comment and aborts the run
A draft-pr issue can never be retried: the auto/N-slug branch survives the worktree removal and every later attempt fails at git checkout -b
With TRIAGE_REPO set to another repository, reviews and draft pushes use git origin's code while gh comments on TRIAGE_REPO
storybench/policybench 'guardrail_fired' counts every guardrail decision, including pass-throughs where the hook added nothing
listing_then_read misses Read-tool reads after a relative ls, because it compares the Read tool's absolute path with the listing's relative one
The guardrail answers the question its pattern names, not the question the search asks: grep intent needs a mapping to graph queries and answer shapes
A devkb query on a repository with no graph prints a Python traceback instead of one line saying to build first
The guardrail records what each search asks (its intent) and the graph question it used, and the stats count every decision
A keyword or a word in another case is never answered as a symbol, and option values are never read as the search pattern
Each search intent gets the graph question that answers it: a body, a definition, a file's outline or grep-like call sites, and nothing for counts, file lists and literals
An answer added beside a search carries only its content, as grep-like lines, and is never larger than grep's own output
Agents are shown, at the moment of intent, the devkb command that answers it, and two direct-path candidates are measured beside the hook
Every benchmark arm starts from a checkout whose own test suite is green, so a red suite is the agent's, not the setup's
The release table shows each arm's spread and marks differences within run-to-run noise, with 3 runs per arm by default
Every scored benchmark run records which version of the hidden check scored it, and runs scored by different checks are never compared
The release performance check is one reproducible command: old/new/new-again passes, machine load recorded, noise marked
Each benchmark arm uses the devkb it claims (release or main), built from an exact commit and recorded in the result
Two builds of the same tree give different flow STEP orders, so graphs cannot be compared
The benchmark records the turns and output tokens of a run's last message only, and counts devkb self-tests as devkb use
A suite that fails only under load scores the run as red, and the failed tests are not recorded
An answer names the devkb command that gives it by default (D1 on)
